category: hosted bot (Telegram file to link, open source)

free_tier.stated: Free, no account: 'Files To Links Fast', with its implementation published at github.com/musa-42/streamer_file. No quota is stated.

per_object_cap.stated: Not published. Telegram's 2 GB per object is the only documented ceiling.

retention.stated: Not stated. The file remains in its chat; the link's lifetime is the operator's.

egress.terms: Free HTTP links; no allowance stated.

interface_detail: A Telegram chat; the source is public, so the bot can also be run by a user instead of used hosted.
tooling: Hosted bot today; the linked repository makes a self-run copy possible on a free VM.
chaining: The only member of the file-to-URL class with public source, so a hosted outage has a fallback: run the same code on a free compute tier.

limits.value: 2 GB, Telegram's own object ceiling; the bot states none

binding_note: Same reasoning as the other file-to-link bots: no published quota, and the platform ceiling is the only documented wall.

identity_cost.detail: A Telegram account; no bot token needed to use the hosted instance.

reliability_note: Hosted by one operator; the public repository is the mitigation, not a guarantee that the hosted instance matches it.
confidence_note: The description and the repository link are on the bot's page read. The repository's own limits were not read line by line.

evidence.proved: 'Files To Links Fast' with 'https://github.com/musa-42/streamer_file' in the description

notes: Abandon if the repository is deleted or the bot stops resolving. This is the one record in the class where the fallback is verifiable, so it is the one to test first.
